title: The Fox and the Crow
source: Aesop's Fables (public domain), gently retold for bedtime

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Once upon a time, in a sunny meadow at the edge of the woods, there lived a shiny black crow.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: One bright afternoon, the crow spotted something wonderful on a windowsill. A little piece of golden cheese!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: She snatched it up in her beak, flapped away, and settled high on the branch of a tall old oak tree.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Mmmmm... she thought. What a lovely supper this will be.
lines.speech: she thought. What a lovely supper this will be.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Just then, a fox came trotting along the path. His nose twitched. Sniff, sniff. He smelled the cheese.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looked up, and there it was, way up high, in the crow's beak. And the fox began to think of a clever plan.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: Good afternoon, Miss Crow! My, my... how beautiful you look today.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: Your feathers shine like the night sky. And your eyes sparkle, like two little stars.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crow fluffed up her feathers. She had never heard such lovely words.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: A bird so beautiful must surely have the sweetest voice in all the woods. Oh, if only I could hear you sing, just once...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crow felt so proud. She lifted her head, opened her beak wide, and sang out...

lines.speaker: crow
lines.text: Caw! Caw! Caaaw!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And down, down, down fell the cheese... right into the fox's waiting paws.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: Thank you, Miss Crow! You do have a voice. But next time, little one, be careful who you listen to.

lines.speaker: fox
lines.text: Sweet words can be lovely... but they are not always true.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: And with a swish of his bushy tail, the fox trotted off into the woods.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The crow sat on her branch for a long while, thinking.

lines.speaker: crow
lines.text: Hmm. I was so busy listening to nice words, that I forgot to hold on to my supper.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: But the crow was not sad for long. Because now she knew something very important.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Be kind to everyone, and listen to everyone... but think for yourself. And never let a little flattery make you forget what matters.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sun went down, painting the sky pink and gold. The crow flew home to her cosy nest, and tucked her head under her soft black wing.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Far away in the woods, the fox curled up in his den, his bushy tail wrapped around him like a blanket.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stars came out. The meadow grew quiet. And everyone, big and small, drifted off to sleep.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Goodnight, little one. Sweet dreams.
